item.title: Trump 'Probably' Open to Meeting Iran's Pezeshkian
item.description: US President Donald Trump told Fox News he would "probably" be open to meeting his Iranian counterpart, Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York this week. Oil dropped for a fourth day, with Brent set for the longest losing run since June, as traders focus on diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, China Hold AI, Trade Talks Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, speaking after hours of talks with China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng and other officials, said the two sides agreed to set up a dialogue on AI aimed at reaching a common understanding on goals and threats. Bessent's comments on "very successful" talks on AI, trade and investment with his Chinese counterparts came ahead of this week’s summit between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: NZ Says Naval Ships Made ‘Routine’ Transit of Taiwan Strait
item.description: Two New Zealand naval ships that transited the Taiwan Strait late last week were undertaking “routine activity” in international waters, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Withers

item.title: Ukrainians Are Bracing for Worst Wartime Winter of Airstrikes
item.description: Ukrainians are already drawing up contingency plans for what threatens to be the worst wartime winter yet.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Verbianyi and Olesia Safronova

item.title: What Career Should You Choose in the AI Age?
item.description: Merryn Somerset Webb speaks with Daniel Susskind, senior research associate at the Institute for Ethics in AI at the University of Oxford and a member of the UK government’s expert panel on artificial intelligence and the future of work. AI is expected to transform the job market, potentially upending many of the traditional educational pathways that have long led students into established professions. As those routes begin to look increasingly uncertain, how should young people prepare for the world of work that awaits them? In his book, What Should My Children Do?, Susskind seeks to answer that question, offering a framework for how children — and adults — can best prepare for an evolving labor market with AI at its center. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Carney, Lula Urge Nations to Join Group to Unite Middle Powers
item.description: Leaders from Canada, Brazil, Kenya and the European Union unveiled a joint diplomatic front on the eve of the United Nations General Assembly, seeking to shield global cooperation from an increasingly transactional geopolitical order.
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: China’s Selective Crop Buying Tests US Trade Truce Before Summit
item.description: China is over halfway to meeting its pledge to buy 25 million tons of US soybeans this year, but progress on a separate commitment to spend billions of dollars more on American crops has largely stalled.
item.dc:creator: Hallie Gu and Erin Ailworth

item.title: Microsoft’s Nadella to Join OpenAI, Nvidia CEOs at Trump-Xi Meal
item.description: Microsoft Corp. Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella is planning to attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping this coming week, according to a person familiar with the planning, joining leaders at Apple Inc., OpenAI and Nvidia Corp.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: F-35 Parts Diversion to Hong Kong Under Probe in US Congress
item.description: A US House committee that oversees defense policy is investigating the diversion of potentially sensitive F-35 fighter jet components this year from Australia to Hong Kong, a spokesperson said.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: China Rare-Earth Magnet Exports to US Drop Before Xi-Trump Meet
item.description: China’s exports of rare-earth magnets to the US fell last month, ahead of a meeting between the leaders of the countries that will probably involve discussions on flows of critical minerals.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: US and China Hail Constructive Talks on AI, Trade Before Summit
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent lauded “very successful” talks with his Chinese counterparts on artificial intelligence, trade and investment, while China described the discussions as positive ahead of this week’s summit between leaders Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan, Yash Roy, Sabrina Mao and Alicia Diaz

item.title: Man Shot by ICE Agent in Austin, Texas, Sparking Mayor’s Ire
item.description: A man shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer Sunday in Austin, Texas, is in “stable, but serious condition,” in the latest incident tied to the Trump administration’s aggressive push to deport undocumented people.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Australia’s Labor Government Extends Slide in Opinion Polls
item.description: Support for Australia’s center-left government fell to a new low as approval for Prime Minister Anthony Albanese weakened, according to a new poll.
item.dc:creator: Nasteho Said and James Mayger

item.title: Trump’s Envoy Works With the UN While His Boss Bashes It
item.description: President Donald Trump derided the UN last year as a worthless institution that “wasn’t there for us.” After a year on the job, his top envoy to the world body has made clear it may have its uses after all.
item.dc:creator: Magdalena Del Valle

item.title: Canada, France to Develop Space Systems as Carney Eyes EU
item.description: Canada and France have asked their space agencies and defense departments to develop and share infrastructure including space-launch systems, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on a visit to a French territory near Newfoundland and Labrador.
item.dc:creator: Paula Sambo

item.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy Will Meet Trump During UN Events in New York
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he’ll meet President Donald Trump during the UN General Assembly week in New York as the embattled Ukrainian leader looks to shore up support to defend against stepped up Russian attacks.
item.dc:creator: Tony Czuczka

item.title: Putin’s Ruling Party Wins Big in Controlled Parliament Vote
item.description: Russia’s ruling United Russia party scored an overwhelming victory in the country’s first parliamentary elections since the start of the war in Ukraine, in a vote tightly controlled by the Kremlin and with virtually no genuine opposition on the ballot.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: German Anti-Capitalists See Mamdani Moment in Berlin Vote
item.description: Germany’s anti-capitalist Left party, which pledged to expropriate housing from private real estate companies, has won an election in the city-state of Berlin, beating both the ruling Conservatives of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and the far-right Alternative for Germany.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Rauwald and Michael Nienaber

item.title: Merz Vows to Stay On After Record German Election Defeat
item.description: Friedrich Merz said he would stay put as German chancellor even after his party suffered its worst-ever result in a state election, with a tally showing the conservatives crashing out of a regional assembly for the first time in the country’s post-World War II history.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs, Michael Nienaber and Kamil Kowalcze

item.title: US, China Meet for Talks in New York Before Trump-Xi Summit
item.description: US and Chinese officials met in New York to lay the groundwork for a high-profile summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, as the world’s two biggest economies seek to maintain — and potentially extend — a fragile trade truce.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan, Yash Roy and Alicia Diaz
